_comment: All deck copy lives here. Edit text freely, then rebuild with: uv run python scripts/marketing/generate_crm_deck.py — see docs/marketing/README.md. Slide numbers are computed automatically, so slides can be reordered, added or removed without renumbering anything.

meta.footer: Notion Pilot · CRM automation for Notion
meta.docSubject: Replacing a spreadsheet CRM with Notion, maintained by AI under human control
meta.docKeywords: Notion, CRM, MCP, automation, self-hosted, pipeline

slides.hero: Stop maintaining your CRM.|Start trusting it.
slides.tagline: Capture anywhere → Structure in Notion → Maintain with AI assistants under human control
slides.footer: Self-hosted · human-in-the-loop · Notion stays the source of truth
slides.purpose: Set the executive promise before introducing any product detail.
slides.notes: Open with CRM adoption and data freshness, not product features.

slides.hero: Your pipeline is a spreadsheet nobody trusts after Tuesday
slides.support: Excel never crashes. It just quietly goes out of date.
rows: As fresh as their last free hour
Rows that don't know each other
Company, contact and deal history never join up
Numbers arrive late — and get argued with
Per-seat cost, rigid workflows, same stale data
slides.purpose: Start from the spreadsheet CRM the audience actually runs today.
slides.notes: Excel is the baseline; the last row is the bridge, not the main point. Not a guaranteed Salesforce replacement.

slides.hero: Notion is already a database. Let's make it your CRM.
slides.support: Companies, People, Deals — linked, with the context on the same page.
slides.callout: Relations keep the three in sync — one company, one contact, one pipeline, no retyping.
slides.purpose: Show that Notion is a credible, flexible CRM foundation.
slides.notes: Notion is the system of record; some deployments label Deals as Leads.

slides.support: Every record joins up — a call logged today shows on the deal, the contact and the company.
hub: Stage · value · probability · expected close · stale flag
slides.callout: Notion Pilot reads and writes the four automated databases. Meetings stays human — and the default deploy creates only three.
slides.purpose: Show the full CRM data model and which parts Notion Pilot actually maintains.
slides.notes: Five databases, not four: Meetings is a real database, related from Activities.Meeting and People.Meetings. A meeting is ALSO an Activity type — both are true. Notion Pilot automates Companies/People/Leads/Activities; the public deploy currently creates only Companies/People/Leads. See docs/notion-pilot-crm-readiness-audit.md.

slides.hero: One workspace. Every deal, with its whole story attached.
slides.support: Account history stops being a scavenger hunt.
rows: CRM in one tool, notes elsewhere
Records and context in one place
slides.purpose: Demonstrate how Notion unifies pipeline, projects, and customer context.
slides.notes: Sell the Notion CRM vision for executives.

slides.hero: The weekly report that builds itself
slides.support: Rollups and formulas do the arithmetic. Views do the layout.
rows: Rollup on the Deals view, grouped by stage
Formula over Closed Won / Closed Lost
Formula on last-activity date, surfaced in a view
slides.callout: Every edit recomputes the numbers. Charts and dashboards are configuration work — not defaults.
slides.purpose: Answer the strongest spreadsheet objection — reporting — with native Notion mechanics.
slides.notes: Excel's charts are what people miss most. Dashboards are configuration work — do not promise a BI product.

slides.hero: Your data, in your region, under your IT's rules
slides.support: All of this comes from your Notion plan — confirm current terms with Notion.
rows: EU data residency is an Enterprise option — to be confirmed with Notion
Shared pipeline views without a per-seat CRM licence
Access governance owned by IT, not by the CRM
slides.purpose: Address data-residency and governance questions before they derail the discussion.
slides.notes: Residency is a Notion Enterprise capability, not a Notion Pilot claim. Never state a guarantee from this deck — point to Notion's current terms.

slides.hero: The challenge is not managing a CRM. It is keeping the CRM alive.
slides.support: Customer data is born in a call. It dies on the way to the form.
slides.purpose: Pivot from Notion as foundation to the CRM maintenance problem.
slides.notes: Notion solves collaboration; Notion Pilot solves maintenance.

slides.hero: Notion Pilot does the typing. You keep the judgement.
slides.support: Self-hosted on your own server. Not a SaaS, not an autonomous agent.
slides.quote: “The AI proposes. The operator validates. Notion remains the source of truth.”
slides.caption: Self-hosted end to end — no third-party SaaS sits between your team and your Notion workspace.
slides.purpose: Introduce Notion Pilot as the operator-controlled automation layer.
slides.notes: Operator-owned infrastructure that makes a Notion CRM sustainable.

slides.hero: The CRM comes to your team, not the other way round
slides.support: Telegram is the most mature surface today.
chat: Preview ready — 1 new Deal, 1 matched Company. Confirm?
slides.purpose: Show where teams capture CRM information in daily workflows.
slides.notes: MCP details in appendix A1. The conversation panel is an illustration, not a screenshot — say so if asked.

slides.hero: Fast automation that creates duplicates is just faster mess
slides.support: Matching runs before the write; anything ambiguous goes to a human.
slides.purpose: Prove that data quality improves before records reach Notion.

slides.hero: One message on Monday. A closed deal with its whole history.
slides.support: Won or lost — the reasoning stays attached.
slides.input_caption: One Telegram message. No form, no fields, no tab-switching.
output: J. Martin — role and email filled
slides.outcome_note: Both outcomes keep the reasoning attached — "why did we lose this" is a search next year, not a memory.
slides.purpose: Walk through one end-to-end deal lifecycle from capture to close.

slides.hero: Nothing gets written that you haven't seen
slides.support: MCP writes require explicit confirmation; Notion stays the source of truth.
slides.purpose: Build executive trust through honest, transparent positioning.

slides.hero: One channel. One entity. Four weeks.
slides.support: At the end you have one pipeline view leadership actually trusts.
steps: One capture source — Telegram or an MCP-aware assistant.
Companies, People, Deals, plus enrichment where it earns its place.
Live pilot with operator review on every single write.
slides.callout: The ask: pick the capture channel and the first entity type before we leave the room.
slides.purpose: Close with a concrete, low-risk pilot plan the audience can act on.
slides.notes: Offer to scope the pilot in a follow-up conversation.

slides.hero: Let's run your next real deal through it
slides.support: One scoping call, then a four-week pilot on your own workspace. Nothing to migrate, nothing to sign.
need: A Notion workspace — Enterprise if residency matters
One capture channel to start with
One named owner for config and review
Two hours of a salesperson's time
slides.get_title: What you have in four weeks
get: Your CRM schema live in Notion
One capture flow running every day
Dedup and enrichment on real records

slides.notes: Translate MCP as safe AI-assisted CRM access.

slides.support: Honest operational model for IT decision-makers.
chips: Python 3.12 · uv · Docker/systemd · FastAPI web cockpit
Notion API + optional OAuth; secrets via Infisical or equivalent
Optional: OpenRouter, Apollo, Brave, Prosper, email/discord
Self-hosted instance controls automation; Notion is system of record
No unsupported certification or residency claims
slides.purpose: Describe the self-hosted deployment stack and operational responsibilities.
slides.notes: Teams manage config, secrets, and monitoring.

slides.support: Confirm naming approval before external use.
chips: B2B CRM: Companies, People, Leads/Deals, Activities
French open-data enrichment for company records
Telegram + MCP for daily capture and maintenance
Activities logged against deals and contacts
Deployment pattern — not a published ROI case study
slides.purpose: Illustrate a real deployment pattern without inventing customer metrics.

chips: Default deploy creates: Companies, People, Leads
Activities and Meetings exist in Notion but are not created by the deploy
Notion Pilot writes Activities once its database id is configured
Meetings is maintained by humans — no tool writes to it
Reporting via Notion views, rollups, and formulas
slides.purpose: Clarify default CRM bootstrap vs optional extended databases.
slides.notes: Do not present extensions as universal defaults.
